skip: Skip any time: Skip in Mags's card, or the menu on the tasks card. One confirm: "Skip Mags's tasks? You keep every reward you've claimed."
Skipping hides the spotlights and the tasks card. Tasks still tick off quietly in the background.
Tapping outside the spotlight never blocks the game: the spotlight fades and the task waits in the tasks card with a Show me button.
resume: Turn Mags back on from Settings or the small Mags button on the Village screen. She starts at the first unfinished task.
Already did it? A task completes the moment the game sees it done (e.g. Farm already level 2). Nobody repeats work.
Rewards wait in the tasks card until claimed and never expire. If the Storehouse is full, Claim shows "Storehouse full: claim later" so nothing goes to waste.
timers: When a task needs something to finish first (Town Hall, Barracks, Raiders, marching), the tasks card shows a countdown and Mags suggests something useful meanwhile.
Tutorial raids and scouting target abandoned villages only, so beginner protection is never lost by following Mags.

practiceRaid.note: With today's numbers a normal level-1 abandoned village (4 Pikemen, 2 Shieldbearers, militia 20 = 170 defence) beats or bleeds 5 Raiders (200 attack): 3-5 of them die. Proposal: each new village gets a "practice ruin" within 2 fields with a garrison of 1 Pikeman + 1 Shieldbearer (defence 80). Then 5 Raiders always win, lose 1, and bring home 120 loot.

steps.title: Welcome, Chief

lines.say: Chief Aren! I'm Mags, the village tinker. Ten little jobs and you'll know how this place ticks. Every job pays.

steps.highlight: No spotlight: the village dims behind a welcome card. Old Orm (the chieftain just picked) and Mags side by side.

trigger.detail: Player taps Let's go on the welcome card (fires once, right after the chieftain is chosen at sign-up: POST /api/me/chieftain).

steps.title: Upgrade the Lumber Camp

lines.say: Everything here is built from wood, so wood comes first.
lines.tap: Tap the Lumber Camp by the trees.

lines.say: Level 2 cuts 35 wood an hour instead of 30. Costs 63 wood, 50 food, 38 iron.
Chop chop! It's on the build list and done in 1m 18s.

steps.highlight: Lumber Camp on the village scene, then the Upgrade to level 2 button in the building panel.

trigger.detail: POST /api/villages/:id/build {building:"lumber"} succeeds (job in queue). Already at level 2 or higher: completes on its own.

steps.completes: When the upgrade starts (no need to wait for it to finish).

steps.title: Upgrade the Farm

lines.say: Troops eat food. Every soldier, every hour, home or away.
Level 2 grows 47 food an hour instead of 40. A fed army is a happy army.
Lovely. Two builds can wait in line at once, so keep that list busy.

steps.highlight: Farm on the scene, then Upgrade to level 2. The queue card now shows two jobs (both slots in use).

steps.title: Build the Barracks

lines.say: Troops train in the Barracks, but that plot opens at Town Hall level 2.
A bigger Hall also builds everything a little faster.
That takes 1m 59s. Have a poke around while you wait. I'll wave when it's done.
lines.tap: Tap Next when the Hall is ready.

lines.say: Hall's done! The Barracks plot is open now.
Costs 200 wood, 150 food, 120 iron. Ready in 2m 53s.
Hammers out! Your first soldiers are close now.

steps.highlight: Town Hall, its Upgrade button, then the empty Barracks plot (Build sign) and Build Barracks. While the Hall builds, the tracker shows a countdown instead of a spotlight.

trigger.detail: Sub-task 1: Town Hall reaches level 2 (job finished; Barracks requires hall 2 current level). Sub-task 2: POST build {building:"barracks"} succeeds.

steps.title: Train 5 Raiders

lines.say: Raiders need a level 2 Barracks. Costs 252 wood, 189 food, 151 iron.
Barracks 2 is up. Time to hire some muscle.
Raiders hit hard and carry loot home. Each one eats 1 food an hour, and your Farm can cover 5.
Five Raiders, ready in 8m 37s. They train one by one.

steps.highlight: Barracks Upgrade to level 2, then Train troops, then the Raider row (count 5) and Train 5 Raiders.

trigger.detail: Sub-task 1: Barracks reaches level 2 (Raider requires barracks 2). Sub-task 2: POST /api/villages/:id/train {unit:"raider", count>=5} succeeds; batches add up.

steps.completes: When 5 Raiders are in training (or already at home).

steps.title: Raid an abandoned village

lines.say: While they train, let's look over the fence.
That grey ruin next door is abandoned. A couple of guards and a full storeroom.
Raiding abandoned villages is fair game, and it won't end your protection.
All 5 Raiders, on attack. They'll be there in 14m 9s.
They're off! I'll shout when the report's in.

steps.highlight: Map tab, the nearest abandoned village (13|-41, 1.4 fields away), Send troops in its popover, then Send 5 Raiders in the send panel.

trigger.detail: POST /api/villages/:id/send {mission:"attack"} at an abandoned village succeeds. Waits for 5 Raiders at home first (tracker countdown).

steps.title: Read the battle report

lines.say: Your Raiders are home and the report's in.
You won, but lost a Raider. They had a Shieldbearer we never saw coming. Bottom row: 30 of each, carried home.

steps.highlight: Reports tab (badge 1), the unread report row, then the losses row and the loot row inside the report.

trigger.detail: GET /api/reports/:id for the raid report (marks it read).

steps.title: Scout before you raid

lines.say: Guessing costs Raiders. A Pathfinder sneaks in and counts theirs. Costs 35 wood, 30 food, 25 iron.
lines.tap: In the Barracks, set 1 Pathfinder and tap Train.

lines.say: Next ruin: 10|-42. Scout is picked, so only the Pathfinder goes. Back with news in 9m 26s.
4 Pikemen and 2 Shieldbearers. That would eat your 4 Raiders. Glad we looked!

steps.highlight: Pathfinder row in Train troops; on the map the ruin at 10|-42, Send troops, and the Scout mission switch.

trigger.detail: Sub-task 1: train.queued {unit:"pathfinder"}. Sub-task 2: send {mission:"scout"} to an abandoned village. Completes when that scout report is opened.

steps.completes: When the scout report is opened (the lesson is reading the intel).

steps.title: Join or found a tribe

lines.say: Nobody wins alone out here. Tribes share warnings, send help and plan raids together.
Open tribes take you straight away. Rather lead? Found your own once your Town Hall reaches level 3.

steps.highlight: Tribe tab, then the Join button on an open tribe. Found a tribe shows its Town Hall 3 lock until then.

trigger.detail: Player becomes a member of any tribe: POST /api/tribes/:id/join, an accepted application or invite, or POST /api/tribes (found). An application alone does not complete it; step 10 unlocks anyway.

steps.completes: When the player is in a tribe.

steps.title: You're on your own

lines.say: That's the lot, Chief! For 2d 22h no player can attack you. Raiding abandoned villages keeps that shield. Attacking or scouting a player ends it early.

steps.highlight: The Protected 2d 22h chip next to the chieftain in the top bar, then the wrap-up card.

trigger.detail: Player taps Off you go. Mags keeps giving tips; she warns about the shield at 24 h and 1 h left, and about every incoming attack after that.

nextSteps: Keep both build slots busy, day and night.
Raid abandoned villages often, and scout first.
Before the shield drops: build a Wall, train Pikemen and Shieldbearers.
Grow the Storehouse and Hidden Vault so raiders find less.
